name: Full Binary Tree Queries
description: You have a full binary tree having infinite levels. Each node has an initial value. If a node has value x , then its left child has value 2· x and its right child has value 2· x + 1 . The value of the root is 1 . You need to answer Q queries. There are 3 types of queries: Cyclically shift the values of all nodes on the same level as node with value X by K units. (The values/nodes of any other level are not affected). Cyclically shift the nodes on the same level as node with value X by K units. (The subtrees of these nodes will move along with them). Print the value of every node encountered on the simple path from the node with value X to the root. Positive K implies right cyclic shift and negative K implies left cyclic shift. It is guaranteed that atleast one type 3 query is present.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer Q ( 1 ≤ Q ≤ 10 5 ). Then Q queries follow, one per line: Queries of type 1 and 2 have the following format: T X K ( 1 ≤ T ≤ 2 ; 1 ≤ X ≤ 10 18 ; 0 ≤ | K | ≤ 10 18 ), where T is type of the query. Queries of type 3 have the following format: 3 X ( 1 ≤ X ≤ 10 18 ).
output_specification: For each query of type 3 , print the values of all nodes encountered in descending order.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 960D — Full Binary Tree Queries [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
